Although the processing technology of small holes by ultrafast laser can greatly improve the quality, there are still problems such as large taper and porthole defects in thesidewall recast layer.¹³In order tofurther improve the processing quality, researchers have carried out much work on the optimization of the hole-making process from the perspective of laser parameters choosing,1hybrid lasers,15,16shielding gas,17and auxiliary medium such as water,1718-20etc. However, most of the works above are based on the one-step drilling method,which has inherent flaws. When the one-step method is used in drilling deep holes, since there is no channel for discharging molten material before the hole is drilled through, the chip removal conditions deteriorate as the processing depth increases,and even with the use of auxiliary high-pressure gases, the spatter cannot be blown completely out of the holes promptly, and there is a serious heat accumulation in the material of porthole and sidewall.21,22As

a result, there are obvious collapsed edges and heat-affected zones around the porthole. Meanwhile, the molten material adheres and condenses on the sidewall of the microhole, forming a thick recast layer with several thermal defects,such as microcracks and oxidation skin, which will reduce the service life of the blade.

For resolving the problems above in the one-step method, a five-axis femtosecond laser helical drilling optical platform is built,and multistep drilling based on a single laser spot and multistep milling methods based on a circular laser beam for microhole processing on nickel-based superalloy were proposed in this work.Because the diameters of the film cooling holes of turbine blades are generally 0.3-1.2 mm,this work chose the small hole with adiameterof 0.4mm to explain the multistep drillingidea and chose the relatively larger hole with a diameter of 0.8 mm to elaborate on the multistep milling approach, respectively.
